items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Sherman wanted to put me in a concert behind Vladimir Horowitz.

ctx.x: That’s a big piece that has not been written about, so that’s an important one. The last thing I wanted to cover today was what appears to be a turning point in your career in 1943 and that’s the Orchestra Hall concert. Can you tell me how that came about?

Joe Sherman wanted to put me in a concert behind Vladimir Horowitz. So I played by myself and he hit me on the behind and he said, “Go out there and lead with your left.” So I played and it was a major success.
Who else was on that bill?
